issues.legal_issue: Intermittent working of a coal mine, with unproved possession during periods when mining ceased, is insufficient to establish title by adverse possession.
material_facts: The claimants’ predecessors entered land leased to the opposing title holders and opened mine workings.
Mining occurred during several separate periods, with substantial intervals in which there were no mining operations.
No other possession by the claimants or their predecessors during those intervals was proved.
The claimants relied on their possession to assert that they had acquired title by adverse possession.
issues.conclusion: The intermittent mining did not establish the continuous possession necessary for adverse possession. Because possession during the periods when mining had ceased was not proved, the presumption that possession reverted to the true owner was not rebutted.
issues.legal_principle: Adverse possession requires open and hostile possession, continuous for the prescribed period; although a mine need not be worked continuously, continuous possession of the mining area and mine is necessary. In the circumstances considered, cessation of operations without proof of other possession left unrebutted the presumption that possession reverted to the true owner. Nageshwar Bux Roy v. Bengal Coal Co. (1930) was distinguished because the claimant there openly asserted rights across the village, sank pits in multiple locations, and acted as possessor of all the minerals. Secretary of State for India v. Debendra Lal Khan (1933) was distinguished because it concerned a fishery, where the nature of possession may differ and acts of possession need not cover every moment of the period. The Court referred to the twelve-year period and Article 144 of the Limitation Act in discussing the authorities.

rule.if: coal_mine_title_dispute and intermittent_mining_operations and not possession_during_stoppages_proved

predicates.coal_mine_title_dispute: The dispute concerns a claim to title by adverse possession over land containing a coal mine.
predicates.intermittent_mining_operations: The claimant or the claimant’s predecessor worked the mine in separate periods rather than continuously.
predicates.possession_during_stoppages_proved: The claimant or the claimant’s predecessor proved possession of the mine or mining area during periods when mining operations had ceased.

issues.definition: When a coal-mine title dispute involves intermittent mining and no proved possession during stoppages, the intermittent operations do not establish adverse possession.
